title: Explain quantity semantics
after: quantity: Integer from 1 through 99. Updating this field replaces the current cart-item quantity; use the remove operation to delete an item.
why: The revision adds range, update semantics, and the correct removal path.

title: Explain nullable money
after: priceBeforeMarkdown is null when no original price is recorded. When present, it contains INR minor units and must be at least the current price.
why: Optional presence and nullable value are different; the new wording explains the actual output.

title: Avoid universal GraphQL status claims
after: Inspect HTTP status and the GraphQL data/errors envelope. Request and transport failures can use non-200 statuses; execution may return partial data.
why: The original collapses transport and execution behavior into an incorrect universal rule.

title: Clarify idempotent retry
before: Try the order again with a new key.
after: For the same order intent after an uncertain result, reuse the original idempotency key and identical details while the server retains that result.
why: New keys identify new intents and undermine duplicate protection.

title: State ownership
before: Use a token to get any cart.
after: Use the cart owner's customer token or the administrator token. Another customer's token is not authorized to retrieve this cart.
why: Authentication alone does not grant resource access.

title: Correct PUT/PATCH advice
before: PUT and PATCH both update whatever fields you send.
after: PUT replaces the writable product representation and requires its mandatory fields. PATCH changes only supplied fields and preserves omitted values.
why: The revision distinguishes replacement from partial modification.

title: Make an error actionable
after: Quantity must be an integer from 1 through 99. Correct the input; do not retry the same invalid request unchanged.
why: It names the field, rule, and recovery instead of merely restating failure.

title: Scope an exact response
after: After a reset and with no intervening order creation, the first new order uses ord_1002. General clients must use the ID returned by their own request.
why: Examples should not turn seeded sequence behavior into a universal contract.

title: Separate return from refund
after: createReturn records one whole-order return request for a delivered order. The local demo does not process refunds or arrange return shipping.
why: The original invents side effects not implemented by the API.

title: Explain pagination stability
after: Use endCursor unchanged with the same filters and sorting. This demo uses offset-backed cursors, so catalogue changes can cause repeats or skips.
why: Opaque cursor syntax does not imply snapshot consistency.

title: Fix a generated-docs claim
before: The OpenAPI renderer is the complete developer guide.
after: The renderer provides a contract reference. Add quickstarts, workflows, conceptual explanations, and troubleshooting for a complete documentation set.
why: Tool-generated reference cannot supply absent task context.

title: Report tests honestly
before: All GraphQL tests passed even though installation failed.
after: GraphQL execution tests were skipped because the runtime dependencies could not be installed. The included tests can run after npm install in a network-enabled environment.
why: A transparent limitation is preferable to fabricated verification.
